 Editorial: Welcome Philippine Airlines. You exemplify why Chicago O’Hare must fight to maintain its dual hub. 
 Long taxis we can live with. A lost One World hub would be a disaster.

 By The Editorial Board | Chicago Tribune PUBLISHED: November 11, 2026 at 5:00 AM CST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... We heard about the new non-stop flight from Chicago O’Hare to Manila from Philippine Airlines some weeks ago, but Mayor Brandon Johnson was part of an official event Monday night, so a welcome to this new international carrier at our big airport seems timely.
 More timely than some flights turn out to be.
 As regular travelers know all too well, taxi times at our big airport have ballooned into experiences that sometimes match the in-the-air time of a short-haul flight. To some degree, this is the price we pay for the plethora of flight choices at Chicago O’Hare. While the taxi time to the terminal from runway 9C/27C, especially, can feel like you landed in Milwaukee, flyers have to remember that without the new and reconfigured runways you might not be arriving at all, especially in rough weather. Last Friday afternoon, for example, the New York airspace was effectively shut down by air traffic control reacting to, well, pretty much just rain. In general, Chicago has avoided these delays.
 But the construction of the new Global Terminal has, of course, made these taxi times much worse, offering a reminder that when city government says there will be minimal disruption, it is best to be skeptical. But here again, that’s the cost of the spiffy new airport under construction.
 We understood why the Federal Aviation Administration started limiting flights at O’Hare effective last June. And we were glad to see that international carriers were not asked to be a part of those caps.
 Long-haul international carriers, crucial to the city’s global connectivity, typically have only a single flight a day, except for the likes of London and Mexico City. We need them. Badly. United and American Airlines, with their myriad short-haul flights, rightly bore the brunt of what we hope will be temporary cuts.
 That brings us to the arrival of Philippine Airlines and the new, thrice-weekly non-stop to Manila. This is especially welcome not just because it serves this city’s Filipino community (the nation’s fifth largest) but because Chicagoans headed to Australia, New Zealand or many other places in the Southern hemisphere can now skip the torture of LAX and get much closer to their final destination.
 There is no mystery why Philippine Airlines has arrived now. On June 6, it joined the One World alliance. That means it can offer seamless connectivity with American Airlines, which has a hub in Chicago. Many of those passengers won’t begin or end their journeys at O’Hare; the American hub will give Philippine Airlines access to the whole Eastern half of the country.
 Scott Kirby, the colorful United CEO, has given a dizzying number of interviews of late, often pushing his self-serving notion that ORD should be a one-hub airport. We enjoy all the good copy Kirby provides. But, as we have written before, this is pernicious and anti-competitive nonsense.
 Philippine Airlines would not be flying here were it not for the presence of a One World hub. Kirby, of course, knows that very well. He would rather people flew United to Manila, but that realistically means changing planes in San Francisco.
 We’d rather go non-stop, thanks. And we’ll wager a whole lot of Filipino-Chicagoans agree with us.
